svg.text: VariLab | coordinate stopping is not a maximum certificate
Exact-rational Hessian inertia separates a saddle, a singular boundary and strict negative curvature.
H_ii = -1 / (1 - m_i^2), H_ij = J_ij. Binary floats become exact rationals before Hessian arithmetic.
Counts share one scale: 45 pixels per eigenvalue. Congruence preserves signs, not eigenvalue magnitudes.
No eigenvalue threshold: the two neighbors of J=1 have different certified signs. Full rational certificates embedded.
Curvature alone does not certify stationarity, an optimum, marginal accuracy or calibrated uncertainty.
